# Strong in the Broken Places
## Scripture
"But he said to me, 'My grace is sufficient for you, for my power is made perfect in weakness.' Therefore I will boast all the more gladly of my weaknesses, so that the power of Christ may rest upon me." – 2 Corinthians 12:9
## Reflection
Most of us were taught that strength means never showing cracks—never admitting the injury, the doubt, the failure. So we grit our teeth, hide the limp, and perform toughness. But Paul discovered something counterintuitive: God's power doesn't flow through the man who pretends he's got it all together. It flows through the man honest about his weakness. Paul begged God three times to remove his "thorn." God's answer wasn't relief—it was relationship. "My grace is sufficient." Brothers, your weakness is not disqualifying. It's the very doorway God uses to display His strength in you. A man who masks his brokenness builds a wall around himself; a man who brings it to Christ builds an altar. Today, stop pretending. Name the area where you feel inadequate—your marriage, your finances, your temper, your faith—and hand it to God. Real strength isn't the absence of weakness. It's the presence of Christ in it.
## Daily Challenge
Do 3 sets of 10 slow, controlled pushups. On the last rep of each set, when your arms shake, whisper, "Your grace is sufficient."
